$description: Canonical colour source of truth. Hand-edit this file only; everything under dist/ is generated by scripts/build_colors.py.

meta.name: F055
meta.naming: shadcn/ui v4 semantic token names, so the web output is drop-in for any Tailwind v4 project.

background.note: Page surface. The Paper artboards render light mode on neutral.100 as a canvas backdrop; the declared --background swatch is white.

popover.note: Not declared in the reference. Mirrors card.

popover-foreground.note: Not declared in the reference. Mirrors card-foreground.

primary.note: Dark mode intentionally steps one notch DARKER than light, confirmed in both the swatch card and live buttons.

secondary.note: Secondary is the one slot on a zinc (cool) ramp rather than neutral. Kept faithful to the reference.

muted-foreground.note: The light value is DARKENED one step from the extracted neutral.500. Reversed on 2026-10-24 after scripts/check_contrast.py measured every text node in all 40 previews: the extracted value is 4.74:1 on card but 4.35:1 on muted and 4.24:1 on input, both under the 4.5 AA floor, and 22 of the 30 failures were that pair. The first reading was that this is a rounding-level miss worth prohibiting rather than fixing; the measurement showed the pair is idiomatic -- avatar initials, chip initials, card labels, placeholder text -- so prohibiting it would have meant redesigning seven components to avoid a value the system leans on. neutral.600 clears every surface (7.81 card, 7.17 muted, 6.98 input) and is close to what Material uses for secondary text; shadcn ships the lighter value and carries the same shortfall. Dark is unchanged: neutral.400 already measures 5.86:1 on muted.

accent.note: Identical to muted in the reference. Kept as a separate token so hover/active states can diverge later.

accent-foreground.note: The ink for anything sitting on `muted` or `accent` -- 18.16:1 light, 14.50:1 dark. This is the system's answer to secondary text inside a muted container, which `muted-foreground` cannot carry at AA: use this and let size or weight carry the hierarchy instead of colour. The pairing existed from the first extraction and went unused until the dashboard hit the problem on a tab strip.

destructive.note: Same value in both themes since 2026-10-24. It used to step to red.500 in dark, which left a destructive button's OWN LABEL at 3.48:1 -- the control was unreadable, not merely low-contrast. red.600 carries white at 4.77:1 in both themes and still clears 3:1 as a fill (4.77 on white, 3.76 on the dark card). Destructive TEXT on a muted or accent surface is a separate case and still measures 4.38:1: do not put it there -- a destructive row hovers to `muted-subtle`, not `accent`. OPEN DECISION remains. The reference never declares destructive — 'Danger Zone' uses plain foreground. Because the brand is red, destructive and primary collide. These values sit one step brighter than primary so they read as hotter, but a non-red destructive (amber/orange) is the stronger option if destructive actions need to be unmistakable.

destructive-text.note: Destructive used as INK on a neutral surface: an error message, a destructive menu item, an invalid field's label. Split from `destructive` on 2026-10-24 because one token cannot do both jobs in dark mode -- a FILL has to be dark enough for white ink to read on it (red.600, 4.77:1), while INK has to be bright enough to read on a dark page (red.500: 5.20 on background, 4.71 on card). Holding both at red.600 left every error message in dark mode at 3.76-4.15:1. Same shape as the chart/series split. On `muted` or `accent` it measures 4.38 light and 3.97 dark, so it does not go there: a destructive row shows hover as an inset `destructive` ring, not a tint -- the ring-not-tint rule Validation and Toast already follow.

destructive-foreground.note: White, not red.50. On a red.600 fill red.50 gives 4.36:1 -- under AA for a 14px/500 button label -- and white gives 4.77:1. The two are visually indistinguishable at label size; only one of them passes.

border.note: Dark border is a white alpha, not a solid neutral — it must stay alpha so it composites over card and background alike.

border-strong.note: The outline of a small control that has to be IDENTIFIABLE: an unchecked checkbox or radio, an unselected segment. `border` is decorative and measures 1.26:1 on card and 1.16:1 on muted in light mode, so a control outlined in it is invisible and fails WCAG 1.4.11, which asks 3:1 for anything needed to identify a component. Nothing in the palette sits between the two: neutral.400 reaches only 2.58:1 on card. So this is the same value as muted-foreground (4.74 / 4.35 / 4.24 on card, muted and input; 6.94 dark on card), aliased under its own name so the intent is explicit and the rule is checkable. Use `border` for separators and decorative hairlines, `border-strong` for anything a person has to see in order to operate.

input.note: Light value measured off the Name/Message fields (neutral.200 at 50%), used as a FILL with a transparent border. Dark value is derived; verify against the dark board before shipping.

muted-subtle.note: `muted` at 50% in both themes - measured as #F5F5F580 light and #26262680 dark. The fill for a row or disclosure item sitting on a card: ListGroup rows, Accordion items, and the settings rows in the reference all use it. One step lighter than `muted`, which is what keeps a stack of rows from reading as a wall of grey.

track.note: The empty half of a slider, and the fill of an unchecked checkbox or radio - the off state of a control. Measured as #E5E5E5E6 light and #FFFFFF22 dark, which is a third alpha ramp distinct from both border (10% dark) and input (15% dark). The values are extracted; only the name is mine.

ring.note: No focus ring is drawn in the reference, so both values are decisions rather than extractions. Dark steps UP to red.500 (the opposite direction from primary) to clear the 3:1 non-text minimum on every dark surface: 5.20:1 on background, 4.71:1 on card, 3.97:1 on muted. Always pair with ring-offset - against primary or destructive the ring is near-invisible without the offset gap, since those surfaces are red too.

ring-offset.note: The gap between a control and its focus ring. Tracks background by design, so the ring always sits on the page colour rather than on the control. This is what makes a focus ring legible on a primary or destructive button, where ring and surface are both red (1.00:1 without it).

chart-1.note: SEQUENTIAL ramp, step 1 of 5 - the step NEAREST the surface, meaning the lowest value. The dark ramp is the light one reversed, which is what makes the scale read the same way in both themes: contrast against the surface climbs monotonically from 1.92:1 to 8.36:1 in light and from 2.15:1 to 9.34:1 in dark. Before 2026-10-24 these five were theme-invariant, which left chart-1 at 1.87:1 on light and chart-4/5 at 2.71:1 and 2.08:1 on dark - unusable at either end. Use for magnitude only: heatmaps, intensity, a single series. For categories use series-*.

chart-3.note: Sequential step 3 of 5 - the midpoint, and the only step whose value is the same in both themes.

chart-5.note: Sequential step 5 of 5 - the most prominent step, the highest value. See chart-1.

series-1.note: CATEGORICAL slot 1 of 3, and the only one carrying the brand hue. Assign slots in order and never cycle them: colour follows the entity, not its rank, so a filter that removes a series must not repaint the survivors. Validated all-pairs: worst CVD separation 11.3 deltaE deutan (light) / 13.1 (dark) against a target of 8, normal-vision 21.4 / 24.8 against a floor of 15, and all three slots clear 3:1 on card in both themes.

series-2.note: CATEGORICAL slot 2 of 3 - full ink. A one-hue system has no second hue to reach for, so the second series is carried by weight instead. Identical in value to `foreground`, aliased separately so a chart does not have to borrow a text token.

series-3.note: CATEGORICAL slot 3 of 3 - muted ink. THIS SLOT REQUIRES A DISTINCT MARK TYPE (dashed against solid, hollow against filled). It is the same value as `muted-foreground`, which is also what axis labels and legend text wear, so hue alone cannot separate this series from the chart's own furniture. There is no slot 4: the palette has one hue, and a fourth series must fold into 'Other' or become a facet.
